solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Judge, a right attack dog?

parts.note: a dog trained to attack is, playfully, one that bites: a biter

explanation.surface: A puzzled question whether a referee is really just a fierce dog set on people.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'attack dog' is a whimsical description rather than a dictionary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an arbiter decides disputes, as a judge does.

clue.text: Bad deal limiting support, it's claimed

indicators.note: limiting says the rearranged letters enclose the other piece
bad says the letters of deal are spoiled and rearranged

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair

explanation.surface: A poor agreement is said to restrict financial support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' gives the anagram ALED, which 'limiting' wraps round the support.
explanation.definitionFit: Something described as supposed, but not proven, is what someone says is so.

clue.text: Don't tell anyone — like most of the characters in Youth Training Scheme

definitions.meaning: a phrase meaning this is confidential

definitions.text: like most of the characters in Youth Training Scheme
definitions.meaning: the scheme's name starts with Y and ends with ME, so nearly all its letters sit in between those

explanation.surface: A confidential aside about a government job scheme for young people.
explanation.walkthrough: The Youth Training Scheme was a 1980s UK programme for school-leavers; read literally, its letters lie between the Y and the ME.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom asking that a confidence be kept secret.

clue.text: Rent to collect on paintings?

parts.note: to reap is to gather in a harvest
paintings are art

explanation.surface: A landlord collecting rent from an art collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like a payment, but is the past participle of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent is the old past tense of rend, meaning ripped into pieces.

clue.text: Means of transport requiring some bread

definitions.meaning: a ...-Royce car, often just called by its short name

explanation.surface: A vehicle that runs on bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rolls-Royce car is called a Rolls; small bread loaves are also rolls.

clue.text: Hold me back, facing two of them!

indicators.note: back says the word me is written in reverse order

parts.note: a brace is a pair, two of something

explanation.surface: Someone cries out to be restrained before taking on a pair of opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to embrace someone is to hold them in your arms.

clue.text: Out there playing with struggling side

indicators.note: playing says the letters of there are put into play and rearranged
struggling says the letters of side are thrown about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sports report: a struggling team on the field over there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges THERE to ETHER; 'struggling' rearranges SIDE to ISED.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient made unconscious with ether, the old anaesthetic, is knocked out.

clue.text: Jack propping up bar with old instrument

indicators.note: in a down answer, propping up puts this letter below the piece before it

parts.note: to bar is to ban
J is short for jack in cards

explanation.surface: An old sailor, Jack, leans against a pub bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A banjo is a stringed musical instrument with a round drum body.

clue.text: Unknown supporting partner seeding man with rail rolling stock business

indicators.note: in a down answer, supporting puts this letter beneath the rest
seeding says this piece is planted inside the other
rolling says the letters of man and rail tumble into a new order

parts.note: a husband is a marriage partner
Y is an algebra unknown

explanation.surface: A farming tale: a spouse sowing seed while a man moves rolling stock along a railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolling' makes the anagram ANIMALR, and 'seeding' plants the partner just before its R. 'Rolling stock' in the surface is railway wagons, a misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Livestock farming, the breeding and care of farm animals, is a business in stock.

clue.text: Intellectual dispute raged as to whether this was big or little end

definitions.text: dispute raged as to whether this was big or little end
definitions.meaning: in Gulliver's Travels, Lilliput and Blefuscu fight over which end of a boiled egg to break

explanation.surface: A scholar recalling a fierce quarrel over which end mattered.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a highbrow; read literally, it is the top of an egg.

clue.text: Former monarch and family entering Nordic parliament in creative approach to problem

parts.note: late means former, as in 'the late chairman'
R is short for rex or regina, a king or queen

indicators.note: entering says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Althing is the parliament of Iceland
kin means family or relatives

explanation.surface: A historical scene: an ex-king and his relatives troop into an Icelandic assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' signals the insertion. The Althing, Iceland's parliament, is one of the oldest in the world; the family goes between its N and G.
explanation.definitionFit: The term, coined by Edward de Bono, names solving puzzles by indirect, imaginative reasoning.

clue.text: Film star informally getting share of meagre takings

indicators.note: share of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A movie star, by casual report, earns only a small cut of a poor box office.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft definition included 'getting', but that word only links the definition to the wordplay; the star is defined by 'Film star informally' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbo, the Swedish screen legend, is referred to casually by her first name.

clue.text: Substitute gets wicket after county's last pair out for duck

indicators.note: after places the county piece ahead of the wicket
the final two letters of the county are removed and something else is put in their place

parts.note: Surrey is an English county south of London
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, so it gives O
a wicket is a small gate, as in a wicket gate

explanation.surface: Cricket talk: a replacement player takes a wicket after the county's tail is dismissed cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: SURREY loses its last pair EY, replaced by O, giving SURRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a surrogate stands in for another person, a substitute.

clue.text: One-piece swimming gear in seaside surroundings

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters sit inside the other piece

parts.note: dunes are sandhills found around beaches

indicators.note: swimming suggests letters moving about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A beach scene: swimwear all in one piece worn amid the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' makes the anagram GARE, which 'in' places inside the sandhills. 'One-piece' suggests a swimsuit but is the bib-and-brace work garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Overalls with a bib are a single garment, a one-piece outfit of trousers and top joined.

clue.text: Poor clue the setter'll need time to clear up

indicators.note: poor says the letters of clue are badly arranged and must be reordered

parts.note: the setter is I, so the setter will becomes I will; the I is used
a date is a point in time

explanation.surface: The setter admits a weak clue will take time to explain.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to elucidate is to explain or make clear.

clue.text: Expressed satisfaction with 0-0, held after goal finally ruled out

parts.note: a goalless score supplies two letter Os

indicators.note: ruled out says a letter is struck from the word held
finally picks the closing letter of goal

explanation.surface: A football fan is content with a goalless draw after a goal is disallowed.
explanation.walkthrough: HELD without the L that ends 'goal' leaves HED.
explanation.definitionFit: To make sounds of pleasure or admiration is to show that one is pleased.

clue.text: Finished with little woman you'd once made ecstatic

parts.note: over means finished
Jo March is one of the sisters in Little Women
ye'd is an archaic form of you'd

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a past love who once delighted them.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: thrilled and delighted, as a person made ecstatic is.

clue.text: Grub used to catch small perch

indicators.note: catch says one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: to root is to dig or grub about, as a pig does for food

explanation.surface: An angler uses a grub as bait to land a little perch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perch' looks like the fish, but is the bird's resting place.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a roost is where birds settle, a perch.

clue.text: Make over balance diocese raised

parts.note: the rest is the balance, what remains

indicators.note: in a down answer, raised says the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and diocese in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Church finances: tidying the books after a diocese raises funds.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something a makeover is to give it a new style.

clue.text: Like rocket lacking oil and not in gear

definitions.meaning: a salad leaf with no oil dressing on it

explanation.surface: A space rocket short of fuel and stuck out of gear.
explanation.walkthrough: Rocket here is the salad leaf, also called arugula, not a spacecraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad with no dressing and a person without clothes are both described with this word.

clue.text: Split up police officers' union

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors
a band is something that binds or unites, as a wedding band

explanation.surface: A police union breaks apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a group that disbands breaks up and disperses.

clue.text: Paradise has crumbled, with wrath endlessly intruding

indicators.note: intruding says one piece forces its way into the other
crumbled says the letters of has fall apart and are rearranged
endlessly says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: acting with wrath is acting angrily

explanation.surface: An idyll falls apart as fury bursts in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumbled' makes the anagram SHA, and 'endlessly' drops the last letter Y before 'intruding' puts the rest in after SH.
explanation.definitionFit: The hidden valley in James Hilton's Lost Horizon became a byword for an earthly utopia.

clue.text: Mounted a horse, when astride beginning to hack in the country

indicators.note: astride says the outer piece straddles the letter inside it
in a down answer, mounted says the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a nag is an old horse

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of hack

explanation.surface: A rider mounts a horse and starts to hack out across the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounted' turns A NAG into GANA; 'astride' puts the H of hack inside it. To hack is to ride out at an easy pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghana is a country in West Africa.

clue.text: Serpentine sunbather in summer?

definitions.meaning: a snake that basks in the sun, Britain's only venomous one
read as one who sums, someone adding figures

explanation.surface: A snake lounging in the sun during the warm season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' is not the season: it is a person who does sums. The Serpentine is also a lake in London's Hyde Park.
explanation.definitionFit: The adder is a common European viper; also one who adds is a summer.

clue.text: Genet, Cocteau etc put these on

definitions.meaning: Jean Genet and Jean Cocteau share the French first name, so they are a group of men so called
denim trousers are something one puts on

explanation.surface: French writers dressing for the day.
explanation.definitionFit: The French given name pluralised is also the denim trousers people wear.

clue.text: Three times a critical time for action turned into meaningless chatter

indicators.note: turned says the whole string of letters is read backwards

parts.words: Three times a critical time for action
parts.note: D-Day is the day a planned operation begins, so 'a D-Day' written out three times in a row

explanation.surface: A rhetorical claim that a decisive moment became empty talk, three times over.
explanation.walkthrough: A plus DDAY reversed gives YADDA, and 'Three times' repeats it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a dismissive term for tedious, empty talk, like blah blah blah.

clue.text: Most of team having ace time stuck in lift

indicators.note: stuck in says these letters are put inside the other piece
most of says the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a football or cricket team is an eleven
A is short for ace in cards

explanation.surface: Most of a team, plus their star player, trapped in an elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: ELEVEN without its last letter gives ELEVE, with AT placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as verbs: to elevate something is to raise it up.

clue.text: Got new shades again, conserving energy, showing the effects of a bad night?

definitions.text: showing the effects of a bad night

indicators.note: conserving says the first piece keeps the other inside it

parts.note: colouring something a second time is to have redyed it
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone recolours their hair after a sleepless night.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloodshot eyes after missed sleep or a late flight are the look of a poor night's rest.
